reason: Against any server that handles the PIPELINING it advertises, sendMail()/SMTPConnection.send() results (accepted, rejected, errors) are the same as before by design, and nodemailer has no option to turn pipelining off, so client code has nothing to write differently; only a non-compliant server (not application code) can tell the difference.

Tried a bulk-spool task (one message, envelope of ~104k subscribers via streamTransport): on 8.0.10 such messages were not workable (about 48 s to build a 100,001-recipient envelope, 26 s for 50k Bcc, and a stack overflow in MimeNode._parseAddresses at about 110k+), so no working pre-cutoff code relied on the uncapped default and a stale variant cannot pass on the old version within the 60 s budget.

Exercising it needs Prisma Client executing a chunked statement against a real database where a later chunk fails, i.e. a database server (or a native SQLite driver adapter, which can't install with --ignore-scripts).

It only changes the file name `prisma init` scaffolds; the pinned CLI still loads a hand-written prisma.config.ts (checked with @prisma/config's loadConfigFromFile), so nothing an agent writes depends on which name init would have used.

Only the error class for an invalid Date in $queryRaw/$executeRaw changes (7.9.0 already turned the 7.8 null binding into an error, a fix outside the population); tried an endpoint mapping PrismaClientValidationError to 400, but any correct pre-cutoff solution validates the Date itself and passes on both versions, so only error-class handling on malformed input could tell them apart.
A raised minimum Node.js version (>=20) with no API change; the template already runs on Node 22.

Prisma Studio is a local dev-server UI started from the CLI; its bind address and CORS headers affect only how a developer opens it in a browser, not any code an agent writes in the project (and running it needs a database and a browser).
